name: Pan American
label: Kranky
lede: The guitarist from the band Kranky was founded to release went off on his own in 1997, recorded his unborn son's heartbeat, lost his father and mother, and is still making Kranky records nearly three decades on.

eras.title: The band a label was built for
eras.text: Mark Nelson sang and played guitar in Labradford, the Richmond, Virginia band whose debut was the reason Kranky existed at all. In the summer of 1997 he started a side project for the music that was too electronic for Labradford.

years.src: Bandcamp Daily: Kranky at 25 · Chicago Reader · Wikipedia: Kranky
years.h: Kranky starts in Chicago to release Mark Nelson's band Labradford
years.p: Joel Leoschke and Bruce Adams found Kranky in 1993 to put out [[Labradford|7cf7ef41-9637-4bf2-ae99-d8d6611ccdc6]]'s Prazision LP, catalog number krank 001. Mark Nelson's band is the label's first release.
years.xp: Both founders worked at the Chicago distributor Cargo, where Labradford's self-released 7-inch landed on Leoschke's desk. Labradford, with [[Carter Brown|f6aba14e-3ab2-4f4c-b729-814dd97609c7]] and [[Robert Donne|dbcf7f68-2f46-4825-a534-bd6227d00605]], made six albums for Kranky between 1993 and 2001.

years.h: Mark Nelson starts Pan American alongside Labradford
years.p: Nelson begins a solo project of electronics, dub rhythms and guitar, often styled Pan•American. Exclaim! says it was for material too electronic for Labradford.

eras.title: Dub, drift and a little help from Low
eras.text: Pan American's first four albums all came out on Kranky, running beside Labradford's last records. By the late 1990s the Labradford members were spread between Richmond, Washington and Chicago, and Nelson's own project grew into his main outlet.

years.src: Chicago Reader: Kranky and Proud of It · Wikipedia
years.h: Pan American: Mark Nelson's self-titled Kranky debut
years.p: The Chicago Reader heard delicate guitar lines and mournful organ swells laid over dub grooves.

years.h: 360 Business/360 Bypass with Rob Mazurek and Low
years.p: Pan American's second album brings in Chicago cornetist [[Rob Mazurek|73c34525-f9c6-4c33-9abe-007748aaebe5]], and [[Low|42faad37-8aaa-42e4-a300-5a7dae79ed24]]'s [[Alan Sparhawk|36aa434c-6823-44b7-b5a6-53bde476c642]] and [[Mimi Parker|31e0783a-9c5d-4218-9f23-4b9427b111e7]] sing on the track Code.

years.h: Labradford releases Fixed::Context, its last record to date
years.p: Mark Nelson's band makes its sixth album with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] and then goes quiet without ever announcing a split. Pan American becomes Nelson's main project.

years.h: The River Made No Sound: Pan American's third Kranky album
years.p: Mark Nelson's first Pan American album after Labradford went silent.

years.h: Quiet City: Mark Nelson brings in Chicago players
years.p: Pan American's fourth Kranky album features Charles Kim, Vandermark 5 drummer Tim Mulvenna and David Max Crawford.

eras.title: A heartbeat on the record
eras.text: Mark Nelson became a father, and the first Pan American record after that carried the sound of his son before he was born. It came out in Austria, the only Pan American studio album of the era not on Kranky.

years.h: For Waiting, For Chasing: his unborn son's heartbeat on every track
years.p: Mark Nelson releases Pan American's fifth album on the Austrian electronic label Mosz. Field recordings of his son's prenatal heartbeat run through each track.

years.h: White Bird Release: Pan American back on Kranky
years.p: Mark Nelson returns to Kranky five years after Quiet City.

eras.title: A band for one record, then Anjou
eras.text: For one album Pan American was a real band, with Chicago drummer Steven Hess of Locrian as a full member and Labradford's Robert Donne on bass. The three then turned into a new Kranky group, Anjou, and Pan American went dormant.

years.h: Cloud Room, Glass Room: Steven Hess joins Pan American
years.p: Drummer [[Steven Hess|f6e3c48b-fe51-42b0-b002-9d77da680442]] is a full member for the first time, and Robert Donne plays bass. Fluid Radio heard a band instead of a solo project.

years.h: Anjou: Mark Nelson, Robert Donne and Steven Hess on Kranky
years.p: Two-thirds of Labradford plus Pan American's drummer release Anjou, the result of four years' work on digital and analog synths. A second album, Epithymía, follows in 2017.
years.xp: The Chicago Reader later wrote that Pan American went dormant while Nelson worked on Anjou and focused on family. Hess went on to the Chicago duo Cleared with Michael Vallera.

eras.title: A son, a father
eras.text: Pan American came back as Mark Nelson alone, recording at home in Evanston, Illinois, with guitars and a hammered dulcimer in place of drum machines. The records turned toward transition and loss.

years.h: A Son: Pan American's first album in six years
years.p: Mark Nelson wrote and recorded it at home in Evanston, then refined it on a European tour. The closer is a solo take on Shenandoah.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Nelson began playing Shenandoah after the 2017 Charlottesville attack as a tribute to Heather Heyer, the woman killed there. The Chicago Reader noted pieces for hammered dulcimer and guitar instrumentals in the spirit of Santo & Johnny.

q: I was looking at patience as a type of kindness.
years.src: Sun 13 interview (2022) · Wikipedia: The Patience Fader
years.h: The Patience Fader: made at home while Mark Nelson's father died
years.p: Nelson started it in spring 2020, alone, during the pandemic. His father was dying that summer and COVID kept Nelson to weekly FaceTime calls.
years.xp: There is no singing on the album. Nelson told Sun 13 the songs came out of his daily guitar practice rather than any theme.

years.h: Mimi Parker of Low, a voice on 360 Business, dies at 55
years.p: [[Mimi Parker|31e0783a-9c5d-4218-9f23-4b9427b111e7]], who sang on Pan American's 2000 album with [[Alan Sparhawk|36aa434c-6823-44b7-b5a6-53bde476c642]], dies of ovarian cancer.

eras.title: Kramer, Grigoni and a silver plane
eras.text: Mark Nelson opened Pan American to partners: two albums with Kramer, founder of New York's Shimmy-Disc, and one with Michael Grigoni. Then came the most personal record yet, about parenthood, losing a parent and going home.

years.h: Pan American and Kramer on the revived Shimmy-Disc
years.p: Reverberations of Non-Stop Traffic on Redding Road pairs Mark Nelson's guitar with Kramer's orchestral drones, first pressed as 555 hand-numbered LPs.
years.xp: [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]] founded Shimmy-Disc in New York in 1987 and revived it in 2020 with Joyful Noise Recordings. Nelson called the collaboration an honor.

years.h: New World, Lonely Ride: Pan American with Michael Grigoni
years.p: An instrumental Kranky album built from folk, country, bluegrass and blues forms, about isolation and a divided country. A second Kramer album, Interior of an Edifice Under the Sea, follows on Shimmy-Disc.

years.big: A photo he never saw while she was alive
q: one I never saw when she was alive
years.h: Fly the Ocean in a Silver Plane: Mark Nelson's mother on the cover
years.p: Pan American's Kranky album is about journeys, parenthood and losing a parent. The cover shows Mark Nelson's mother, about to board the silver plane of the title.
years.xp:
Nelson says the record grew from two songs about travel and coming home: Jo Stafford's You Belong to Me and Chuck Berry's Promised Land. He recorded it at home over several years on electric and rubber-bridge acoustic guitar, Ableton Live and a Digitone synth.

Mallory Linnehan of Chelsea Bridge added violin and vocals, recorded at the Not Not space in Chicago. Richmond's Style Weekly marked the release with a long interview.
